facts.text: DeviceConnection is the Lake Shore Model 218 connection class; it handles the instrument over serial over Ethernet
read_all writes the ASCII command KRDG? 0 followed by a newline, reads one line, and returns the decimal numbers its regular expression finds
The written command is KRDG? 0, where the comment says 0 means all channels
The Device class creates one softioc analog-input record per configured channel and creates a DeviceConnection from the ip, port and timeout settings
The sample settings file configures the lakeshore_218 IOC with module devices.ls218 and port 23, channel 1 of a serial-to-Ethernet adapter, with a 2 s timeout
The sample settings file lists eight channel slots for the 218 and publishes only Test_TI, with EGU set to K
TelnetConnection opens telnetlib.Telnet(host, port, timeout) and stores it as self.tn; it defines no close, stop, abort or disable method
The IOC host imports the device module, constructs module.Device(device_name, ioc_settings), calls connect() and then repeatedly awaits device.do_reads()
DeviceConnection has no stop path: the class body is its constructor and read_all, and its base TelnetConnection has only the constructor

measures.description: Channel readings returned by one read_all() (KRDG? 0); the clone states no unit and the array length is the number of channels the instrument answers
measures.name: temperatures

measures.description: Read every channel with one KRDG? 0 query and return the parsed numbers; it changes nothing
measures.name: read_channels

safe_state.description: no actuator is driven by this temperature monitor; the runtime latch refuses effectful commands. The e-stop performs a fresh KRDG? 0 communication check and does not cancel an in-flight read
